Reserve eUSD: bridged collateral and issuance of the existing
pool token
Research date: 29 September 2026. This study examines a conditional architecture against the deployed
copied Reserve v2 contracts. All new chain calls are getters; no governance changes, token issuance,
administrative payloads or state-changing simulations were performed.
Principal findings
The copied eUSD issuer, Main, AssetRegistry and BasketHandler identify themselves as version 2.0.0.
The complete registered token/plugin mapping and prime basket match at the inherited fork boundary
and endpoint snapshot. The active basket contains saUSDC, cUSDC, saUSDT and cUSDT at the exact
addresses recorded below. The existing Curve pool lists the same eUSD contract minted by this issuer.
The deployed issuer accepts the quantities required by its active basket; registration alone does not
make an asset an active basket component. Its verified source distinguishes asset refresh, basket status,
throttle capacity, issuance and collateral transfer. The cached basket status and stale price-feed
observations below do not establish successful issuance at the endpoint.
These reads do not show newly bridged collateral installed in this eUSD basket. Direct e121 role checks
are reported separately from the additional Main and timelock governance-history audit (Appendix 19).
No finding about human ownership or participant intent follows from these reads.
Exact contracts, versions and snapshots
The endpoint is PulseChain chain 369, block 27,659,393, hash 
0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275, 28 September 2026 08:22:35 UTC.
Historical comparison uses the final inherited Ethereum block 17,232,999, hash 
0xe5667f9cafb115b1dcfc36b0b569a5601f01dfa000698140a1298ef4f87e2e37. Each batch checks its chain and rechecks
its block header.

2^192−1), not a usable narrow price estimate. The USDC plugins reference feed 
0x8fffffd4afb6115b954bd326cbe7b4ba576818f6; the USDT plugins reference 
0x3e7d1eab13ad0104d2750b8863b489d65364e32d. Their eight-decimal feed answers are 99,983,300 and
100,074,527, respectively, but their updatedAt values are 1,683,705,647 and 1,683,732,947, both 10

recorded SOUND statuses.
Issuance calls assetRegistry.refresh() before checking the basket. Therefore the cached status, the basket

issuance was simulated here. The core implementation sources are verified; availability of exact plugin
source is different: explorer lookups for all four plugin addresses returned address-only records without
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 117

verified source. Their successful getters therefore support the stated observations, while this study does
not claim a complete source-level proof of each plugin's next refresh behavior. A returned status alone
does not establish economic backing or successful future refresh.
Why a bridged token needs a collateral adapter
The verified registry maps an exact ERC-20 address to an IAsset adapter. toColl additionally requires that
adapter's isCollateral() return true. The adapter supplies the token address and decimals, price bounds,
collateral status, target denomination and reference-unit conversions. Registration calls its refresh logic;
a label such as PRC-20 or ERC-4626 does not supply those semantics on its own. A token can have a
standard transfer interface and still have incompatible collateral behavior.
The basket's target quantities are denominated in target units per basket unit, not arbitrary counts
of bridged shares. A collateral adapter's targetPerRef relates target units to reference units; refPerTok
relates reference units to each whole collateral token. Basket quantities and token decimals then
determine the actual deposited raw integer amounts, with rounding. For yield receipts and bridge
representations, these conversions must reflect the particular claim and its redemption/valuation
semantics. Oracle control alone does not provide the missing underlying asset or validate those claims. 
Asset interfaces and basket conversion code.
A governance-approved adapter and basket configuration could therefore represent a particular L1
bridge receipt backed by escrowed L2 collateral. A mintable bridge representation and an ERC-4626
receipt are candidate asset forms, not universal acceptance classes. The bridge must first deliver a
token on the issuer's chain; Reserve then evaluates and takes custody of that exact token. If a receipt
merely references the same collateral already promised to other independent claims, registering it does
not cure duplicated backing.
Basket governance and actual ownership evidence
In the verified v2 components, the governance modifier checks main.hasRole(OWNER, caller). OWNER is the
right-padded bytes32 ASCII string OWNER, not its hash. Main's public role getters use the _ROLE suffix. The
OWNER role is its own administrator and is also administrator of PAUSER, SHORT_FREEZER and
LONG_FREEZER. The actual getRoleAdmin reads confirm that hierarchy. register, collateral-plugin
replacement and prime-basket changes use this governance boundary; UUPS component upgrade
authorization also uses it. Main Auth and component authorization source.
The examined e121 address, 0x98c89980d1eae247ada3636ae27648f78e66e121, returns false for all four roles. The
same bounded checks return false for the modern upstream documented timelock 
0x7bea807798313fe8f557780dbd6b829c1e3ad560 and governor 0xf4a9288d5deb0eae987e5926795094bf6f4662f8. Those
latter addresses are candidates from upstream documentation, not established PulseChain governance
owners. The initial collateral batch did not enumerate role holders. The subsequent governance audit
(Appendix 19) identifies timelock 0xc8ee187a5e5c9dc9b42414ddf861ffc615446a2c as the sole OWNER in the
returned Main role history and confirms the endpoint getter. Its proposer is Governor Alexios. Neither
direct e121 role checks nor unchanged Main ownership establish who controls voting power in that
governor.
Registry eligibility, configured prime basket and active reference basket are separate states. The verified
source makes setting the prime configuration a governance action; an active-basket switch has its own
conditions. A single-token basket is structurally possible because the configuration requires a nonempty
valid collateral list, not a minimum of two constituents. It does not follow that one arbitrary token can
replace the current four-component deposit without a valid configuration and active-basket transition.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 118

Same-token issuance and conservation of backing
The v2 RT oken's ordinary issueTo path requires a positive amount, an unpaused and unfrozen system,
refreshed assets, a SOUND basket, issuance-throttle capacity and its exchange-rate invariant. For
existing supply S, requested raw eUSD amount M and current required basket units B, it computes the
additional basket requirement as the upward-rounded B × M / S. It asks the active basket for a deposit
quote rounded upward, increases required basket units, mints eUSD to the recipient and transfers every
required basket token from the issuer to BackingManager. A failed transfer reverts the entire
transaction, including the mint. When supply is zero, its initial basket relationship is handled by a
separate branch. Exact issueT o source.
Consequently, a bridged asset included with a partial weight is only one part of the required basket. The
issuer must also supply the other constituents. If an authorized, valid active basket instead consists
solely of that asset, ordinary issuance can use it alone. This changes the collateral composition of the
same RT oken; it does not give the bridge unrestricted mint authority over eUSD. The separate mint
function in this source is restricted to BackingManager and is not a public arbitrary-collateral deposit
function.
At the endpoint, eUSD total supply and basketsNeeded both equal 13,223,010.934604392856634411, in
their respective 18-decimal units. An exact one-basket quote using the v2 CEIL enum value 2 returns
0.229775 saUSDC, 10.94460233 cUSDC, 0.224353 saUSDT and 11.20233014 cUSDT. These are receipt-
token amounts reflecting their reference conversion rates, not four equal counts of USDC/USDT. The first
inventory quote used ROUND enum value 1 only to identify the basket; the retained CEIL quote is the
issuance-relevant rounding convention. A quote is a read-only amount calculation, not an execution
success proof.
issuanceAvailable() returns 1,000,000 eUSD. The configured throttle uses an absolute rate of 1,000,000
eUSD and a supply fraction of 2.5%, with an hourly limit equal to the larger of those two quantities. It is
replenishing issuance-rate capacity, not a lifetime one-million-token maximum, and it does not waive
backing or status checks. The source has governance-bounded throttle configuration, but this study
makes no assumption that e121 can change it. Throttle library and issuer source.
Changing the configured basket does not transport new backing into BackingManager. Existing eUSD
holders retain claims under the protocol while holdings and required composition may diverge.
Rebalancing, collateral status, redemption and any recapitalization rules remain relevant. An intended
new basket must therefore be distinguished from proof that it is funded and redeemable. The theoretical
representation held by Reserve is a claim on the escrowed source asset; those layers do not constitute
two independent pools of free collateral. Selling eUSD transfers the claim to its purchaser, while the
backing commitment continues.
What this resolves, and what remains conditional
There is a coherent positive architecture: a bridge supplies a recognized L1 collateral representation,
Reserve accepts that representation as valid basket collateral, and the existing eUSD issuer creates the
same token already listed in Curve. The exact token-identity obstacle is resolved at the issuer boundary,
not by a shared symbol or by having a bridge call eUSD mint directly.
For the actual sampled deployment, the registered mapping and prime basket remain the inherited
configuration, direct e121 governance authority is absent, and present pricing evidence does not
establish usable refreshed issuance. A specific bridged collateral contract, valid adapter, authorized
configuration, actual backing custody, successful issuance receipt and subsequent public trade would be
needed to turn the conditional architecture into an observed path. None of those missing facts can be
replaced by the assertion that the destination pool lists eUSD. The conditional architecture is separate
from the observed transaction record.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 119

Reproduction and retained evidence
The explicit getter manifests are the six files named Research/experiments/
parb_reserve_collateral_{metadata,roles,plugins,inventory,inherited,feeds}_20260929.json. Use Research/scripts/
probe_pulsechain_routes.py with the explicit --calls manifest, matching --block and a fresh output path. The
inherited manifest uses 0x106f467; all other manifests use 0x1a60c81. Do not substitute the runner's default
experiment mode. Existing outputs are preserved.
Raw responses, verified core sources, source-query results and decoded summary are under ignored 
artifacts/parb-reserve-collateral-20260929/. The initial attempts to call OWNER() and similarly abbreviated role
getters revert; verified source identifies the correct _ROLE() getter names and the later batch records their
successful results. No missing or reverted result is treated as a zero-valued state. Source-fetch failures
are distinct from successful on-chain plugin getters. No production application behavior changed, so no
production test suite was run for this study.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 120

quote rounded upward, increases required basket units, mints eUSD to the recipient and transfers every
required basket token from the issuer to BackingManager. A failed transfer reverts the entire
transaction, including the mint. When supply is zero, its initial basket relationship is handled by a
separate branch. Exact issueT o source.
Consequently, a bridged asset included with a partial weight is only one part of the required basket. The
issuer must also supply the other constituents. If an authorized, valid active basket instead consists
solely of that asset, ordinary issuance can use it alone. This changes the collateral composition of the
same RT oken; it does not give the bridge unrestricted mint authority over eUSD. The separate mint
function in this source is restricted to BackingManager and is not a public arbitrary-collateral deposit
function.
At the endpoint, eUSD total supply and basketsNeeded both equal 13,223,010.934604392856634411, in
their respective 18-decimal units. An exact one-basket quote using the v2 CEIL enum value 2 returns
0.229775 saUSDC, 10.94460233 cUSDC, 0.224353 saUSDT and 11.20233014 cUSDT. These are receipt-
token amounts reflecting their reference conversion rates, not four equal counts of USDC/USDT. The first
inventory quote used ROUND enum value 1 only to identify the basket; the retained CEIL quote is the
issuance-relevant rounding convention. A quote is a read-only amount calculation, not an execution
success proof.
issuanceAvailable() returns 1,000,000 eUSD. The configured throttle uses an absolute rate of 1,000,000
eUSD and a supply fraction of 2.5%, with an hourly limit equal to the larger of those two quantities. It is
replenishing issuance-rate capacity, not a lifetime one-million-token maximum, and it does not waive
backing or status checks. The source has governance-bounded throttle configuration, but this study
makes no assumption that e121 can change it. Throttle library and issuer source.
Changing the configured basket does not transport new backing into BackingManager. Existing eUSD
holders retain claims under the protocol while holdings and required composition may diverge.
Rebalancing, collateral status, redemption and any recapitalization rules remain relevant. An intended
new basket must therefore be distinguished from proof that it is funded and redeemable. The theoretical
representation held by Reserve is a claim on the escrowed source asset; those layers do not constitute
two independent pools of free collateral. Selling eUSD transfers the claim to its purchaser, while the
backing commitment continues.
What this resolves, and what remains conditional
There is a coherent positive architecture: a bridge supplies a recognized L1 collateral representation,
Reserve accepts that representation as valid basket collateral, and the existing eUSD issuer creates the
same token already listed in Curve. The exact token-identity obstacle is resolved at the issuer boundary,
not by a shared symbol or by having a bridge call eUSD mint directly.
For the actual sampled deployment, the registered mapping and prime basket remain the inherited
configuration, direct e121 governance authority is absent, and present pricing evidence does not
establish usable refreshed issuance. A specific bridged collateral contract, valid adapter, authorized
configuration, actual backing custody, successful issuance receipt and subsequent public trade would be
needed to turn the conditional architecture into an observed path. None of those missing facts can be
replaced by the assertion that the destination pool lists eUSD. The conditional architecture is separate
from the observed transaction record.
